definitions.explanation: A roof covered with bundled reeds, straw, or miscanthus grass, traditional on old Japanese farmhouses and shrines.

examples.japanese: この{村|むら}には{茅葺|かやぶ}き{屋根|やね}の{民家|みんか}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Thatched-roof houses still remain in this village.

examples.japanese: {茅葺|かやぶ}き{屋根|やね}は{数十年|すうじゅうねん}ごとに{葺|ふ}き{替|か}える{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: A thatched roof needs to be re-thatched every few decades.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {茅葺|かやぶ}き{屋根|やね}: a thatched roof
- {茅葺|かやぶ}きの{民家|みんか}: a thatched-roof farmhouse

CULTURAL NOTE:
Thatched roofs are emblematic of traditional rural Japan; famous examples survive in the gasshō-style villages of Shirakawa-gō. The kanji {茅|かや} refers to the miscanthus and reed grasses used for thatching, and {葺|ふ}く means to roof or thatch.
